caption:
🤖 Behind the Scenes of My Claude Code Pipeline: One API Call Judges 4 Things About My Content — Using Just 1,503 Tokens

Claude Code can write a full content pipeline in an afternoon. What it can't do on its own is tell you whether the hook is actually good, or whether a diagram will still be legible once it's shrunk to a LinkedIn thumbnail. Jev (TypeSafe AI's System One model) plugs into exactly that gap — not a linter for syntax, a judge for quality, running before anything is allowed to build. Let's break it down.

🔹 How The Judgment Call Actually Works

jev-claude-code.json is the manifest for this exact carousel — six slides, written by hand.

scripts/quality-gate.mjs reads it and builds one structured "state" object: the audience, the hook slide, the CTA slide, every slide's text, every diagram's source.

That state goes into Jev's client.systemOne() as a single call, asking four questions in parallel — hook_strength, cta_is_specific, jargon_risk, diagram_readability.

Jev answers each one with a score or a probability, plus its own confidence — a Noul reading near 0.5 means "I'm not sure," not "the answer is 50%."

Any answer under 0.6 confidence gets downgraded to REVIEW regardless of what it said — a confident bad grade is more useful than an unsure good one.

Only rows marked OK pass silently. FLAG and REVIEW rows print straight to the terminal, and --strict turns either one into exit code 1.

Only after that does scripts/build.mjs even run, turning the same manifest into one self-contained HTML document.

scripts/render.mjs opens that HTML in headless Chromium and exports carousel.pdf plus one PNG per slide — the first time anything actually gets rendered.

All of that — one network call, four parallel judgments, a hard confidence floor — happens before build.mjs writes a single line of HTML.

💡 Why It Actually Works
✅ Judge, not linter — a schema catches malformed JSON; Jev catches a boring hook the schema would happily approve.
✅ Confidence over answers — a low-confidence "good" grade still gets flagged for REVIEW, never trusted blindly.
✅ A separate stage, not middleware — runs before build.mjs, never inside the deterministic render path, so the render pipeline stays fully offline and reproducible whether or not the gate ever runs.

🌍 Where else should an agentic coding pipeline have a judgment layer like this — code review? Commit messages? Something else entirely? Genuinely curious what you'd wire in.
